messages:
maya: Hey team — after upgrading to redwood-inference-sdk@1.2.0 our Next.js production build fails. Local dev works. Build error during Vercel deploy: 

```
  Error: Package exports for 'redwood-inference-sdk' do not define a valid './package.json' subpath
  at new ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED (internal/errors.js:xxx:xx)
  at applyNodeResolution (internal/modules/esm/resolve.js:xxx:xx)
```

My package.json (app):
```
{
  "name": "customer-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "redwood-inference-sdk": "^1.2.0",
    "next": "12.3.0"
  }
}
```

I tried pinning 1.1.9 and build succeeds. Any ideas? (prod only, Next/ESM build) :thinking_face:
messages_2: eric: Thanks @maya — can you paste the SDK package.json from node_modules (the top-level one) and your Node version? Also, does this happen on a fresh install (node_modules cleared + lockfile)?
messages_4: devon: Good catch. For bundlers like Next (SSR), you generally need both `import` and `require` entries inside `exports` or a fallback `main` that points to CJS. The missing `require` export can cause the resolver to fail during certain build modes. Two immediate options: 1) patch the package.json in node_modules locally to add require entry and test, or 2) use a canary release with both fields. I'll loop eng.
messages_6: ci-bot: Published redwood-inference-sdk@1.2.1-canary.20260315 — CI build passed, smoke tests ok. :rocket:
messages_7:
maya: Tried the canary, build moved forward but now fails with: 

```
Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs' in '/vercel/path0/node_modules/redwood-inference-sdk/dist'
```

Stack trace points to a small helper that does `fs.readFileSync` for a local cache — bundler is trying to include it in a browser/edge bundle. This only happens on Next Edge functions. (SSR serverless works). Any workaround?
messages_9:
sarah: Confirmed. We pushed a real patch release 1.2.3 that: 
- adds `require` entry to exports
- guards server-only `fs` call behind dynamic import and `process.browser` checks
- adds `browser` field to package.json mapping to a tiny shim-dist for edge builds
- ensures `types` are exported via `exports."./*"` so TS consumer resolutions work in ESM/CJS scenarios

Release notes: https://internal.redwood/release/1.2.3 (internal link)
messages_10: ci-bot: Published redwood-inference-sdk@1.2.3 — patch release. Changelog: exports map fix, edge/fs guard, types export fixes.
messages_11: maya: Installing 1.2.3 fixed our Vercel production build and Next Edge functions. Types are picked up in TS serverless builds too. Thanks so much!! :tada:
messages_12: alex: Documenting root cause and mitigation: shipping an incomplete `exports` map (missing `require` + no browser shim) caused Next/Edge bundlers to fail. Followup actions: add automated export map lint in CI, add a bundler smoke test using Next edge. Assigning to eng-runtime for test coverage. Thanks everyone.
messages_13: eric: Closing the escalation — please reopen if you see regressions. Logged customer repro and fix under support ticket #S-3241. :white_check_mark:
